title: Free love style test: Lee's six styles of love (Eros, Storge, Agape…) — cv.cm
description: Free love style quiz based on John Alan Lee's six styles: passionate (Eros), playful (Ludus), friendship (Storge), practical (Pragma), possessive (Mania) and selfless (Agape). Rate 24 statements, no sign-up.
h1: Love style test: how do you love?
lede: Do you fall fast and hard, or does love grow slowly from friendship? Rate 24 statements to find your main love style among the six described by sociologist John Alan Lee.
about: In 1973 the sociologist John Alan Lee described six styles of loving, named with Greek and Latin words: Eros (passionate), Ludus (playful), Storge (friendship), Pragma (practical), Mania (possessive) and Agape (selfless). Most people mix several, and the mix can change with age and with each relationship.

The statements here were written for cv.cm and are inspired by Lee's model; this is not the published Love Attitudes Scale. Your result names your strongest style and shows your scores for all six. Different styles can work well together once partners understand each other.

faq.q: What are the six love styles?
faq.a: Eros (passionate, romantic love), Ludus (love as a playful game), Storge (love that grows from friendship), Pragma (practical, well-matched love), Mania (intense, anxious love) and Agape (selfless, giving love).

faq.q: Is one love style the best?
faq.a: No single style is best. Studies link Eros and Agape with more satisfying relationships and Mania with more jealousy and worry, but what matters most is that partners understand each other's style.

faq.q: Is this the same as love languages?
faq.a: No. Love languages are about how you like to give and receive affection. Love styles are about how you approach love itself: how fast you fall, what you look for and how intense it feels.
Yes. Lee saw the styles as attitudes, not fixed traits. They shift with experience, age and the partner you're with.

eros.name: Eros: passionate love
eros.body: You love with your whole heart and trust chemistry: attraction, romance and closeness come first. Passion gives your relationships energy. Keep curiosity and small romantic gestures alive as the first spark settles into something steadier.

ludus.name: Ludus: playful love
ludus.body: You see love as fun, light and full of possibility, and you don't like to be tied down too early. You make dating exciting. Be clear with people about what you're looking for, so nobody gets hurt by different expectations.

storge.name: Storge: friendship love
storge.body: Your love grows slowly from friendship, shared interests and trust. It's calm, loyal and built to last. You may not feel fireworks at first, and that's fine: your strength is a partner who is also your closest friend.

pragma.name: Pragma: practical love
pragma.body: You choose with your head as well as your heart, looking for shared values, goals and a life that fits together. That makes for stable partnerships. Leave room for spontaneity and feeling, too, not just the checklist.

mania.name: Mania: possessive love
mania.body: You love intensely, and that can come with highs, lows, worry and jealousy. Your devotion is real. Building your own sense of security, through friends, interests and honest talks with your partner, helps love feel calmer.

agape.name: Agape: selfless love
agape.body: You love by giving: caring, forgiving and putting the other person first without keeping score. It's a rare gift. Make sure your own needs matter too, and choose partners who give back.
